Rashi on Ketubot 23b:10:1.english: Lest you say, etc. - And [it is] because she is believed regarding herself [that the Tanna] taught it.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:11:1.english: With regard to her, since there are witnesses - We read [this text].

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:11:2.hebrew: היינו רישא דרישא - דהא ודאי משום דאינה נאמנת על עצמה לא אצטריך למיתנייה, דהא טובא אשמועינן דבמקום עדי שבויה לא מהימנא למימר טהורה אני. ומשום נאמנת על חברתה הוא דאצטריך, דאע"ג דעד קא מכחיש לה מהימנא — והא ברישא דרישא אשמעינן:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:11:2.english: This is the first part of the first clause - For certainly, [the Tanna] did not need to teach it because [of the ruling that] she is not believed regarding herself, since [he] has already taught us many times that where there are witnesses of captivity, she is not believed to say "I am pure." Rather, it was needed because [of the ruling that] she is believed regarding her counterpart — that even though a witness contradicts her, she is believed — and he already taught us this in the first part of the first clause.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:12:1.english: Where she renders herself unfit - [It is] there that she is believed regarding her companion, because she says, "I am defiled."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:12:2.english: But where she also renders herself fit - Say [that] it is because of herself that she is speaking, and not regarding her counterpart.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:12:3.english: We read [in the text]: "[it] teaches us."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:12:4.hebrew: <abbr title="לישנא אחרינא">ל"א</abbr> גרסינן: מהו דתימא כי מהימנא במקום עד פסול — כגון דעד דקא מפיך הוי אשה — אבל במקום עד כשר לא; תנא משנה יתירה, <abbr title="דאפילו">דאפי'</abbr> במקום עד כשר:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:12:4.english: Another version: We read [the Gemara text as follows]: What might you have said? When is she believed? Against a disqualified witness — such as where the witness who contradicts [her] is a woman — but against a valid witness, [she is] not [believed]; [therefore, the Tanna] taught an extra Mishnah [clause, to indicate] that even against a valid witness [she is believed].

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:1.english: And likewise, two men - We do not have the reading "who were taken captive."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:2.english: They are not deemed credible - to give them terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:3.english: And when they testify about each other - That each one says, "I and my fellow are priests."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר אין מעלין לכהונה על פי עד אחד - ואפילו היכא דליכא גומלין, וכל שכן הכא דאיכא למיחש לגומלין — "העד אתה עלי ואני עליך":
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: One does not elevate [a man] to the priesthood on the basis of one witness - Even where there is no reciprocity, and all the more so here, where there is [reason] to suspect reciprocity — "Testify for me, and I [will testify] for you."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:5.english: Challengers - [People] who call a name of disqualification against him.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:6.hebrew: מעלין - היכא דליכא גומלין, והיינו דאיכא בין ר' אלעזר לתנא קמא דר' יהודה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:6.english: One elevates [to priesthood] - [Even] where there is no reciprocal [testimony], and this is [the difference] that exists between Rabbi Elazar and the Tanna Kamma [who preceded] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:7.hebrew: רבן שמעון כו' - בגמ' מפרש מאי בינייהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:13:7.english: Rabban Shimon, etc. - In the Gemara, it explains what [the difference] is between them.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:1.hebrew: כל הני - דתנא מתניתין לאשמועינן הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר, ל"ל:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:1.english: All these - that the Mishnah taught to inform us [of the principle that] "the mouth that prohibited is the mouth that permitted," why do I need [them]?

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:2.hebrew: משום דאיכא דררא דממונא - הלכך, אי לאו דפשיטא מלתא שלקחה מאביו, לא היה אומר "של אביך היתה" וגורם לעצמו הפסד ממון. וכשאומר תחלת דבריו, על שם סופו אמרו, לגמור בהן "ולקחתיה הימנו":
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:2.english: Because there is a financial stake - Therefore, were it not clear that he purchased it from his father, he would not say, "It belonged to your father," and [thereby] cause himself a financial loss. And when he says the beginning of his words, he says it with a view to their end, to conclude with them, "and I purchased it from him."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:3.english: However, witnesses - Who said, "It is our handwriting."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:4.hebrew: דליכא דררא דממונא - לגבייהו, דלימטינהו פסידא בהאי עדות:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:4.english: Where there is no financial stake - For them, [such] that a loss would befall them through this testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:5.hebrew: אימא לא - ליתהמנו למימר "אנוסין היינו", דמעיקרא כי אמרו "כתב ידינו הוא", אדעתא דסהדותא אמרו, ולאו למיגמר בה "אנוסים היינו", והדר אימליכו למיגמר בה הכי. קמשמע לן:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:14:5.english: Say no - [that] they should not be believed to say, "We were coerced," for initially when they said, "This is our handwriting," they said [it] with the intention of [giving] testimony, and not to conclude with [it], "We were coerced," and afterwards they reconsidered [and decided] to conclude with it like this. [Therefore, the Mishnah] teaches us [that they are believed].

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:15:1.hebrew: דלעלמא - אין הדבור האחרון מהני לעצמו אלא לאחרים, ומשום אחרים לא הוו הדרי במלתייהו. אבל איהו גופיה, דלנפשיה מהני כי הדר ואמר לקחתיה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:15:1.english: That [it is relevant] to others - The latter statement does not benefit themselves, rather [it benefits] others, and for the sake of others they would not retract their statement. However, [as for] him himself, [it] benefits himself when he retracts and says, "I purchased it."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:1:1.english: Two women who were taken captive - [This refers to a case] where there are witnesses that they were taken captive.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:1:2.english: That they testify about each other - Each one says: "My companion is pure."

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:1:3.english: They are deemed credible - For in [the case of] a captive woman, [the Sages] were lenient to believe one witness, and even a woman.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:2:1.english: She is deemed credible - regarding everything.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:2:2.hebrew: אינה נאמנת - על כלום, ולקמיה מפרש לה לכולה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:2:2.english: She is not deemed credible - regarding anything, and later [the Gemara] explains all of it.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:3:1.english: If there are no witnesses - that they were taken captive.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:3:2.hebrew: אלא פשיטא דאיכא עדים - הלכך, אעצמה אינה נאמנת לטהרה. וחברתה נמי, אע"ג דאנן אמרינן בחזקת טמאה קיימא, ההוא לאו משום הימנותא דהך הוא, דבלאו סהדותא דידה נמי בחזקת טומאה היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:3:2.english: Rather, it is obvious that there are witnesses - Therefore, with regard to herself, she is not deemed credible to declare herself pure. And [regarding] her counterpart as well, even though we say [that] she stands in a presumptive state of impurity, that is not because of the credibility of this [woman], for without her testimony as well, she is in a presumptive state of impurity.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:4:1.hebrew: ואינה נאמנת על חברתה - על כרחך משמע דחברתה בחזקת טהורה קיימא. דבשלמא אינה נאמנת דרישא, אע"ג דאכולה מילתא משמע, שייך למיתנייה משום דידה; אלא הכא, דבהדיא תנא אינה נאמנת על חברתה, קשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:4:1.english: And she is not deemed credible with regard to her counterpart - Perforce, [this] implies that her counterpart stands in a presumptive status of purity. For granted, [with respect to] "she is not deemed credible" of the first clause, even though it implies [that she is not credible] regarding the entire statement, it is appropriate to teach it because of her [own case]; but here, where it explicitly teaches "she is not deemed credible with regard to her counterpart," it is difficult.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:4:2.hebrew: אלא פשיטא דליכא עדים - ואדידה מהימנא, דשויתה לנפשה חתיכה דאיסורא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:4:2.english: Rather, [it is] obvious that there are no witnesses - And regarding herself she is believed, because she has rendered herself a forbidden piece.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:7:1.english: Who reverses - [He] reverses all of her words.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:7:2.english: She rendered herself a forbidden piece - Therefore, the witness is not believed to declare her pure.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:7:3.hebrew: חברתה משתריא אפומא דידה - דבשבויה האמינו חכמים עד אחד להקל, ואפילו עבד או שפחה, כדקתני מתני' (לקמן כתובות דף כז.): אם יש להן עדים, אפילו עבד כו'. וכל מקום שנאמן בו עד אחד הרי הוא כשנים, ואין דברי אחד שכנגדו לטמא עומד במקום שנים:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:7:3.english: Her counterpart is permitted on the basis of her [word] - For in [the case of] a captive woman, the Sages believed one witness to be lenient, even a slave or a maidservant, as the Mishnah teaches (below, Ketubot 27a): "If they have witnesses, even a slave, etc." And wherever one witness is believed, he is [considered] like two [witnesses], and the words of the one who opposes him to declare [her] tainted do not stand in place of two [witnesses].

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:8:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן איהי כיון דאיכא עדים לאו כל כמינה - ואעדי שבוייה קאי, דעד אחד בטומאה אינו כלום אלא בסוטה בלבד, שרגלים לדבר, שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:8:1.english: This is the reading: [As for] her, since there are witnesses, it is not in her power - And [this] refers to the witnesses of [her] captivity, for one witness regarding defilement is nothing except in [the case of] a sotah alone, where there is a basis for the matter, since [her husband] warned her and she secluded herself.

Rashi on Ketubot 23b:9:1.hebrew: היינו רישא - הני מילי תרוייהו אשמעינן ברישא: חתיכה דאיסורא מרישא שמעינן, שריותא דחברתה אפומא דעד מסיפא דרישא שמעינן. תרתי בבי קמייתא רישא קרי להו, דדמיין להדדי, ותרתי בבי בתרייתא חדא מילתא היא; דבכל חדא תנן מילתא וחילופה, בין ברישא בין בסיפא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23b:9:1.english: This is the first clause - Both of these matters were already taught to us in the first clause: [that she renders herself] an entity of prohibition we learn from the beginning of the first clause, [and] the permitting of her counterpart on the basis of [one] witness we learn from the end of the first clause. The first two clauses [the Gemara] calls "the first clause," since they are similar to each other, and the last two clauses are [likewise] one unit, for in each [pair] we taught a case and its opposite, both in the first section and in the latter section.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:14:1.hebrew: דאיכא דררא דממונא - פירש ר"ח שהאומר הוא מוחזק בשדה, אבל העדים אין בידם כלום:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:14:1.english: That there is financial significance [derara demamona] - Rabbeinu Chananel explained that the one who says [this] is in possession of the field, whereas the witnesses have nothing in their possession:

Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:14:2.hebrew: אבל הכא דליכא דררא דממונא לא - קשה לרשב"א: הא איצטריך גבי עדים לאשמועינן דמהימני במגו לפסול השטר, דהא אע"ג דר' מאיר פליג אסיפא, מודה ברישא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:14:2.english: But here, where there is no financial significance, no - It is difficult for Rashba: Behold, [the Mishnah] was needed regarding witnesses to teach us that they are believed through a migo to disqualify the document, for even though Rabbi Meir disagrees regarding the latter clause, he concedes regarding the first clause.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:1:1.hebrew: שתי נשים שנשבו - אומר ר"י, דלא גרסינן "זאת אומרת נשביתי וטהורה אני" כו', אלא "זאת אומרת טהורה אני", דהא בדאיכא עדים שנשבו איירי. ומיהו יש לקיים הגירסא, דאיירי דאינהו לא ידעי דאיכא עדים, ואשמועינן דאפילו הכי לא מהימני:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:1:1.english: Two women who were taken captive - Ri says that we do not read [the text as]: "This [woman] says, 'I was taken captive and I am pure,'" etc., but rather: "This [woman] says, 'I am pure,'" because [the Mishnah] is dealing with a case where there are witnesses that they were taken captive. However, one can uphold the [existing] reading, [explaining] that it is dealing with a case where they do not know that there are witnesses, and it teaches us that even so, they are not believed.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:6:1.hebrew: אין רישא וסיפא דאיכא עדים ומציעתא דליכא עדים - השתא לא פריך: "הא תו למה לי?", כדפריך אשנויא דרב פפא, דהשתא אצטריך כולהו: "אני טהורה וחברתי טמאה" — אשמעינן כיון דאיכא עדים, לא מהימנא אנפשה. "ואני וחברתי טמאה" — אשמעינן דלא מהימנא אחברתה היכא דליכא עדים, ומשתריא חברתה אפומא דנפשה. "ואני וחברתי טהורה" — אשמועינן אע"ג דאיכא עדים מהימנא אחברתה; דרישא, דרישא איכא לאוקמי בדליכא עדים. ואין נראה, דאי בדליכא עדים, היינו מציעתא! אלא בדאיכא עדים איירי, ומ"מ איצטריך האי סיפא לאשמועינן דנאמנת אחברתה, ואע"ג דלא פסלה נפשה והיה לנו לחוש לגומלים, אפילו הכי מהימנא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:6:1.english: Yes, the first clause and the last clause [are] where there are witnesses, and the middle clause [is] where there are no witnesses - Now [the Gemara] does not ask: "Why do I need this additional [clause]?" as it asks on the answer of Rav Pappa, because now all of them are needed: "I am pure and my companion is impure" — it teaches us that since there are witnesses, she is not believed regarding herself. "And I and my companion are impure" — it teaches us that she is not believed regarding her companion where there are no witnesses, and her companion is permitted based on her own statement [that she is pure]. "And I and my companion are pure" — it teaches us that even though there are witnesses, she is believed regarding her companion; [unlike] the first clause, for the first clause can be established where there are no witnesses. However, [this] does not seem [correct], for if [the first clause is] where there are no witnesses, that is [identical to] the middle clause! Rather, [the first clause] deals with a case where there are witnesses, and nevertheless this last clause is needed to teach us that she is believed regarding her companion, and even though she does not disqualify herself and we might have been concerned about reciprocating [mutual favoritism], even so she is believed.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:9:1.hebrew: הא תו למה לי היינו רישא - וא"ת: ואמאי לא קאמר הכא מרישא דרישא כדקאמר בסמוך, דהא שמעינן מרישא דרישא דאיהי שויתה לנפשה חתיכה דאיסורא וחברתה משתריא אפומא דידה, וכ"ש דמשתריא אפומא דעד אחד? וי"ל: דהכא ניחא ליה למנקט סתמא דהיינו רישא, משום דמרישא נמי שמעינן דחברתה משתריא אפומא דעד אחד; אבל בסמוך לא מצי פריך אלא מרישא דרישא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23b:9:1.english: "Why do I [need] this additional [case]? This is [identical to] the first clause!" - And if you should ask: Why does [the Gemara] not say here "[this is identical to] the very first clause," as it says shortly below — for we learn from the very first clause that she rendered herself an entity of prohibition and her counterpart is permitted on the basis of her own word, and all the more so that she is permitted on the basis of one witness? And one can answer: Here it prefers to state simply "this is the first clause," because from the [immediately preceding] first clause as well we learn that her counterpart is permitted on the basis of one witness; whereas shortly below it could only challenge from the very first clause.
